name: Beau Addinsall
summary: Gold Coast academy ball magnet who averaged 32 disposals and nearly 8 clearances in the Talent League, with a 129 junior fantasy average. Clean at stoppages, covers ground and links up in transition. Needed to hurt more with each touch and kick it more often.

name: Daniel Annable
summary: Brisbane academy midfielder rated elite for contested ball and consistency. A clean, one-touch extractor at stoppages who added two-way running and goals, including snaps resting forward. Not quick, and his kicking under pressure and flair needed work.

name: Harley Barker
summary: Modern athletic wingman with speed (a 2.86s 20m) and an aerobic engine who runs both ways and uses the ball well by foot. Strong overhead on the outside. Contested and ground-ball work were the gaps.

name: Sam Cumming
summary: Powerful inside midfielder who also goes forward and marks strongly overhead. Rarely had fewer than 20 touches in the SANFL under-18s and was rated elite for ceiling. Kicking technique and his outside game were the work-ons.

name: Harry Dean
summary: Elite aerial defender who reads the play early and marks or spoils at the drop zone. Tough one-on-one, and a clean left-foot kick out of defence (85% efficiency). In-between size and versatility were the question marks.

name: Lachy Dovaston
summary: Elite-agility small forward who does more than kick goals: he creates turnovers, runs in transition and added midfield and stoppage craft during the year. Small, and his goalkicking accuracy was the main work-on.

name: Cooper Duff-Tytler
summary: Elite-ceiling 201cm ruck-forward with rare agility and mobility for his size. Vic Metro's No.1 ruck but named at centre half-forward in the All-Australian side, and played forward on VFL debut for Essendon. Needs to add strength and refine his ruck craft.

name: Louis Emmett
summary: Mobile 199cm forward and fourth-midfielder ruck with an elite engine (third in the combine 2km). Strong contested marker with a big leap who links up through the ground. Consistency and contest craft were the work-ons.

name: Willem Duursma
summary: Elite-ceiling 193cm utility from a basketball background with outstanding aerial reach, who dominated in the air in defence then became a mobile marking threat forward (16 goals in 13 games). A 94.5 junior fantasy average at the carnival. Contested work and kicking consistency were the work-ons.

name: Jacob Farrow
summary: Powerful half-back with one of the best long kicks in the draft (compared to Hayden Young's left foot) and 89% efficiency at the carnival. Intercepts, rebounds and takes on the game with speed. Defensive craft and endurance were the work-ons.

name: Oliver Greeves
summary: Big-bodied 191cm stoppage midfielder rated elite on contested ball, with clean hands and a powerful kick; 25 disposals and a 92 junior fantasy average for Vic Metro. Also showed outside class and run for Eastern. Below average for speed and endurance.

name: Sam Grlj
summary: Elite-speed, high-ceiling runner who breaks lines from half-back and the midfield with dare and repeat efforts (top 10 in both the combine sprint and 2km). Low accumulator as a junior, and his composure with the ball needed work.

name: Noah Hibbins-Hargreaves
summary: Deadeye forward (82% conversion as a bottom-ager) who is quick on the lead and strong overhead, and added wing and on-ball minutes in his draft year. Elite ceiling. Durability and ground-ball work were the flags.

name: Jack Ison
summary: Carlton academy left-footer: tall, agile midfielder-forward whose kicking inside 50 is a weapon and who has poise in traffic. Can play almost anywhere. Ground-ball work and work rate were the questions.

name: Max King
summary: Sydney academy enigma: a freak 191cm athlete with elite speed (2.83s 20m) and a 98cm running jump who can take a screamer or run the length of the ground. Very raw: low output, poor consistency and ball use, and his finishing and footy IQ needed work. Pure upside, not a fantasy profile yet.

name: Josh Lindsay
summary: Consensus best kick in the draft: a free-roaming half-back with elite vision and decision-making who sets up play with a kick-first game. Teams play for him to get the ball. Contested work and defensive effort were the work-ons. A classic rebounding-defender fantasy type.

name: Archie Ludowyke
summary: Lean, springy 197cm key forward in the Aaron Cadman mould: leads hard, marks at the highest point and kicked over three goals a game. Needed to add strength and become more consistent.

name: Mitch Marsh
summary: Athletic, high-marking 190cm forward who topped the national carnival goalkicking (12 in four games) after two a game in the SANFL under-18s. Steady set shot and long kick. Needed to add strength and consistency.

name: Zac McCarthy
summary: Lightly framed, still-improving 199cm forward who can pinch-hit in the ruck. Big reach overhead and a high-upside long-term type. Needed a lot more strength and to stay on the park.

name: Cameron Nairn
summary: Medium forward who plays above his height, covers big ground and kicks goals: back-to-back 22-goal SANFL under-18 seasons and a seven-goal haul for SA at the carnival. Clinical by foot. Consistency and ground-ball work were the work-ons.

name: Dylan Patterson
summary: Gold Coast academy speedster with elite agility and speed: a daring, line-breaking half-back and midfielder who takes the game on and hurts teams with each possession. High risk, high reward. Composure and endurance were the work-ons.

name: Jevan Phillipou
summary: High-impact midfielder-forward who wins the hard ball, takes big marks for his size and hits the scoreboard; a 91.6 junior fantasy average in the SANFL under-18s. Tested well at the combine (third in the running jump, eighth in agility). Composure and his defensive game needed work.

name: Sullivan Robey
summary: Big, powerful 192cm midfielder-forward with elite strength: a lead-up target forward who is also mobile at ground level in the midfield. Kicked goals in eight of nine Talent League games and averaged 98 fantasy points. Rare dual-position profile; decision-making and limited exposure were the flags.

name: Aidan Schubert
summary: Elite contested-marking 194cm forward who doubles as a second ruck; kicked six against Vic Metro and averaged 94 fantasy points at the carnival. Raw and rangy but competitive. Kicking and composure needed a lot of work.

name: Dyson Sharp
summary: The best contested-ball winner in the crop: SA's captain dominated the carnival with 27 disposals, 11 contested possessions, 6 clearances and 5 tackles a game (106.8 fantasy). Strong, tough and clean in tight, with SANFL League exposure. Kicking and outside game were the work-ons. A ready-made fantasy accumulator profile.

name: Adam Sweid
summary: Resilient small midfielder-forward who lost his bottom-age year to a knee reconstruction, then bounced back with a consistent, high-work-rate 2025. Quick, evasive, tackles hard and wins clearances. Small, and composure was the work-on.

name: Oskar Taylor
summary: Elite-kicking, elite-speed half-back (fastest 20m sprint at the combine, 2.823s) who takes the kick-ins, carves through teams on the rebound and finishes chains inside 50. Consistent and accountable. Contested work and strength were the work-ons.

name: Xavier Taylor
summary: Well-rounded 192cm defender who can lock down talls or smalls, then grew into a star interceptor and rebounder. Elite agility, sub-three-second speed and elite contested work. Decision-making and kicking were the work-ons.

name: Blake Thredgold
summary: Lockdown key defender who thrives on big matchups (held Mitch Marsh goalless in a grand final) and added more intercepting late in the year. Elite in the air and a good athlete. Low ball production and decision-making were the flags.

name: Zeke Uwland
summary: Gold Coast academy all-rounder rated elite for ceiling, consistency and disposal: a smart, hard-running, kick-first player who can play any line and drives transition with lethal foot skills. Already held his own at VFL level. Acceleration and durability were the only real flags.

name: Sam Allen
summary: Endless-tank wingman with elite endurance who roams to find the ball, marks well overhead and hits the scoreboard; also played half-back and forward. Midfield craft and strength were the work-ons.

name: Talor Byrne
summary: Explosive, tough small forward who can push through the midfield, with clean hands, crumbing smarts and a potent left foot. Small and needed a bigger tank.

name: Lachlan Carmichael
summary: Sydney academy playmaking half-back who takes the kick-ins everywhere he goes, intercepts, and uses it efficiently (82%) by foot; 95 junior fantasy average at the carnival. Contested ball and midfield craft were the work-ons. Rebounding-defender fantasy type.

name: Koby Coulson
summary: Gold Coast academy inside midfielder with elite contested work, agility and power: high-production (24 disposals, 5.5 inside 50s) and a dogged two-way competitor. Kicking composure and polish were the work-ons.

name: Cody Curtin
summary: Powerful 200cm key forward (brother of Dan Curtin) with elite strength and contested marking who kicked 32.9 in nine WAFL Colts games, including six in the grand final. Vice-like hands. Not quick, and needed more running power.

name: Jack Dalton
summary: Workhorse running machine, arguably the best endurance athlete in the crop, rated elite for consistency. Came back from a long injury to average 28.5 disposals in the Talent League, with a balanced inside-outside game and six tackles a game at the carnival. Lacks explosive speed. Strong fantasy accumulator profile.

name: Will Darcy
summary: Rangy, skilful 196cm tall in the mould of his brother Sam, with reach, clean hands and mobility to play either end. A raw upside pick with very little junior production or exposure.

name: Finnegan Davis
summary: Rebounding half-back who switched to an attacking role in 2025 and racked up 28 disposals (21 kicks) and 6.4 rebound 50s a game, a 107 junior fantasy average. Also can play as a lockdown defender. Durability and size were the flags. Classic fantasy rebounder.

name: Hussien El Achkar
summary: Classic crumbing small forward who kicked 47 goals in 26 games for Calder over two years, finding the ball at ground level and scoring from anywhere. Can go goalless at times; defensive pressure and endurance were the work-ons.

name: Koby Evans
summary: Big, powerful 188cm forward who moved into the midfield in 2025 and won it inside and out (26.5 disposals, 5 tackles in the Colts). Speed and flair, and kicks goals. Consistency and decision-making were the work-ons.

name: Hunter Holmes
summary: Elite-speed wingman with a big engine who links up in transition and also held his own on-ball, winning clearances despite a light frame. Fast improver. Composure and kicking were the work-ons.

name: Matthew LeRay
summary: All-Australian wingman who has played all four lines and finished the year in defence; a 188cm utility with clean hands on both sides and a strong work rate. Endurance testing was modest and decision-making needed work.

name: Max Kondogiannis
summary: Roaming third-tall interceptor who reads the play early, flies for marks and then runs and kicks the ball out of defence (6 rebound 50s a game at the carnival). Undersized for a key back and his one-on-one craft needed work.

name: Harry Kyle
summary: Sydney academy athlete with a rugby background who drives the ball forward from half-back or the wing with power and repeat running; best running vertical jump at the combine (98cm). Consistency and footy IQ were the work-ons. Upside more than output.

name: Hugo Mikunda
summary: Creative, smart small forward-midfielder who sets up goals more than he kicks them, with clean one-touch hands and dangerous delivery inside 50. Quick with good running power. Defensive pressure and his own scoreboard impact were the work-ons.

name: Jai Murray
summary: Gold Coast academy playmaker who always seems to have time, moving from half-back and wing into an inside midfield role in the Noah Anderson mould: 23 disposals, 7.5 tackles and 6 clearances a game, a 101.5 junior fantasy average. Not quick.

name: Zane Peucker
summary: Explosive, compact small forward with elite speed (2.89s 20m in preseason) and X-factor: hunts the loose ball, breaks tackles and makes things happen in chaos. Composure and endurance were the work-ons.

name: Tyan Prindable
summary: Brisbane academy clearance midfielder who is clean at the stoppage, reads the ruck taps, and tackles hard (about eight a game in the Talent League); held his own at QAFL and VFL level. Average athletically and lacks flair.

name: Noah Roberts-Thomson
summary: Sturdy, clean ball-winning midfielder who can also hurt teams forward or off half-back with a penetrating left foot. Sixth in both the combine sprint and agility, and averaged 98.8 fantasy points in the SANFL under-18s. Impact per possession and defensive transition were the work-ons.

name: Sam Swadling
summary: Arguably the best ball-finder in the draft: a 189cm two-way running midfielder rated elite for consistency who racked up big numbers in the WAFL Colts and can rest forward as a marking target. Ball use and impact per possession were the knocks. Fantasy-friendly accumulator.

name: Avery Thomas
summary: Desperate, brave lockdown defender and elite athlete (elite for leap, agility and speed) who competes above his 185cm in the air and rarely gets beaten one-on-one. Decision-making with the ball and endurance were the work-ons. More a defensive role player than a fantasy scorer.

name: Tylah Williams
summary: Elite-speed, elite-agility small forward (second in the combine 20m sprint, fourth in agility) who works up the ground and back with huge running power and creates in transition. Small, and contested ball was the work-on.

name: Charlie Banfield
summary: West Coast father-son prospect (son of Drew): a 192cm utility who moved from wing and forward into the midfield late in the year and averaged 26.8 disposals across four finals, best afield in Claremont's Colts flag. Won the WA state combine 2km. Kicking polish and speed were the work-ons.

name: Kye Fincher
summary: St Kilda Next Generation Academy graduate: a powerful, daring rebound defender who added midfield minutes and made his VFL debut for the Saints' affiliate. Quick and bold by foot. Composure and stoppage craft were the work-ons.

name: Tai Hayes
summary: Mature-age wingman (nephew of Lenny Hayes) who went from Mornington Peninsula local footy to a QAFL breakout and then the VFL with Southport, where he played every game until an ankle injury. Raking left foot and works hard both ways.

name: Thomas Matthews
summary: Livewire 171cm small forward and Gippsland captain whose draft year was wrecked by a preseason PCL injury, playing only four games. Quick, slick at ground level and relentless with his pressure. Size and durability were the concerns.

name: Latrelle Pickett
summary: Over-age bolter from Port Lincoln (cousin of Kysaiah) who kicked 32 goals in 18 SANFL Reserves games and played three League games for premier Glenelg. Quick, springy and evasive with natural goal sense. Topped SA's state-combine 2km. Defensive work rate was the work-on.
